transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got the draft collateral reinvestment plan on the table -- $25 million into 30-day commercial paper from Delta Financial. Before I authorize anything, I need to hear from each of you in the exception report. Counterparty risk, compliance, client coverage, investment operations -- please give me your one-minute read. If there are no exceptions, I'll authorize the plan as drafted. If there's an issue, bring me a compliant alternative and I can approve a replacement in this same huddle.

transcript.text: Counterparty risk has an exception. I completed a counterparty review this morning confirming that Delta Financial's commercial paper is under active rating review. Until that review closes, desk policy prohibits any new purchase of Delta commercial paper. I recorded the result in my working file, but the counterparty system has not been updated yet, so it wouldn't have flagged in the system check. We cannot proceed with the Delta CP as proposed.

transcript.text: Compliance has an exception. I reviewed the applicable collateral-investment mandate this week and found that the cash collateral may be placed only in government Treasury bills or AAA-rated bank certificates of deposit, each with a maturity of no more than 14 days. This restriction has not yet been added to the desk's pre-trade checklist, which is why it wouldn't have been flagged in the system check. The proposed 30-day commercial paper from Delta Financial violates this mandate on both the instrument type and the maturity dimension. We cannot proceed with the Delta CP as proposed.
